sections.html:
• Similar looking to the Phractura genus.
  • Quite rare in imports.
Africa: Known only from the type locality: Ouesso, Sangha River (middle Congo River basin), Republic of Congo. The species may be more widespread than is currently known.
Found in the banks of rivers with floating and hanging vegetation. They will hide at the river banks among leaves and twigs.

This genus prefers water with a bit of movement as they are found at the margins of swift-flowing streams. Provide floating plants with long stems and branches. Not an easy species to keep due to their high maintenance and their specialised diet.
Small live foods such as sifted Daphnia, Rotifers and Artemia.

Etymology: The specific name sanghensis: -ensis, suffix denoting place: Sangha River, Ouésso, Republic of the Congo, where it is endemic.

There are four species in this genus: T. ineac, T. intermedius, T. minutus and T. sanghensis. Similar looking to T. minutus, of which a few ichthyologists (Pellegrin & Matthes) think T. sanghensis may be a synonym, but the holotype of T. minutus was not in good enough condition to make a definite decision.

IUCN Red List: Data Deficient, but needs updating (IUCN 2010). More information is needed on the species distribution before an assessment can be made.
